clue.text: Plan soldiers exploit to get drink

parts.note: a plan or map of a route is a chart
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: A military scheme to make the most of a supply of liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword stand-in for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a French herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks.

clue.text: Attend to a man aright

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
the word splits as A plus R, the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look after a man properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aright' looks like an adverb meaning correctly, but it breaks into 'a' and 'right' (R).
explanation.definitionFit: To listen to or heed someone is to attend to them, as a judge does a case.

clue.text: Join the assembly, or possibly draw back

explanation.surface: Come along to a gathering, or else pull a curtain away.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up at a gathering is to arrive casually; to furl a blind or sleeve is to pull it back.

clue.text: Having to do with a sound upbringing

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in a business letter
a ring is a sound, as of a bell

explanation.surface: Something about bringing a child up well and healthily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound upbringing' reads as one phrase about good parenting, but 'sound' is RING and 'upbringing' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising children is their nurture or bringing-up.

clue.text: An employer's cunning ruse

indicators.note: cunning suggests a crafty rearrangement of the letters of the word ruse

explanation.surface: A boss's crafty trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunning' looks like it describes the ruse, but it signals the anagram of RUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: One who employs a tool or service makes use of it, so is its consumer.

clue.text: Remove to boot a little weight

parts.note: to boot means in addition, or extra
ct is the abbreviation for carat, a small unit of weight for gems

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take something away and throw in a small weight as well.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something out, such as a tooth, is to take it away.

clue.text: Tease a bungler — popular though shabby guy

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them
a muff is a clumsy person who fumbles things
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Making fun of an incompetent fellow who is well liked despite his scruffy look.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a dirty, ragged person, usually a child.

clue.text: Made a drawer

parts.note: a drawer here is not furniture or an artist but something that draws metal towards itself

explanation.surface: Someone constructed a chest drawer or trained an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron given magnetic properties attracts, or draws, other metal.

clue.text: Drop a lengthy story

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cut out a long tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally an Icelandic heroic tale.

clue.text: Quietly train male rebels for Westminster

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: rebels as a verb suggests the letters of train and male revolt into a new order

explanation.surface: A man is quietly coached to revolt against the British government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebels' looks like a noun, but it is a verb telling the letters of TRAIN MALE to rearrange into ARLIAMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Westminster is the London district housing the UK legislature, and its name stands for it.

clue.text: Keep terriers in check

indicators.note: in places the territorials inside the word for check

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
terriers is old slang for the Territorial Army, TA

explanation.surface: Hold the dogs back on the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terriers' suggests dogs, but it is British slang for the Territorial Army (TA), a volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold on to something is to retain it.

clue.text: States small change in dispatch will cause delay

indicators.note: in tells us the states and the small change go inside the word for dispatch

parts.note: to dispatch is to send
US is the United States
p, a penny, is small change

explanation.surface: Sending American coins will hold things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off or postpone something is to suspend it.

clue.text: Enchanted by the period before spring?

indicators.note: before puts the period ahead of the spring

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Bewitched by the season just before the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season but is a leap (BOUND).
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound means held as if by magic, transfixed.

clue.text: Those contemplating getting pets-cats or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters of pets-cats and or are rearranged

explanation.surface: People thinking about acquiring pets, cats or something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectators are onlookers who watch and contemplate a scene.

clue.text: Exercise a baboon

explanation.surface: Put a monkey through its paces.
explanation.definitionFit: Drill is repetitive military training, and also a West African baboon.

clue.text: Judge a foreign aristocrat to be about 100

indicators.note: about tells us the a and the aristocrat surround the number

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman, not a British title
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Considering a European nobleman to be nearly a centenarian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about 100' seems to mean roughly a hundred, but 'about' puts A COUNT around C.
explanation.definitionFit: To account someone wise is to consider or reckon them so.

clue.text: Animosity is shown by some strangers

indicators.note: some of the word strangers, a run of its letters, is on show

explanation.surface: Some unfamiliar people display hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is hostile feeling or rage.

clue.text: Make allowances for the president

explanation.surface: Making concessions for the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses S. Grant was the 18th US president.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede a point is to make allowance for it; Ulysses Grant was a US president.

clue.text: Were reformed in jug

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of were are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ex-convicts who went straight while in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' is slang for prison, which suits 'reformed', but here it is the definition: a pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large pitcher with a wide mouth.

clue.text: Most fences hold such creatures back

indicators.note: back means the hidden run is read in reverse
hold signals that the words most fences contain the run of letters

explanation.surface: Most garden fences shelter some animals at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: The run STFE hidden in 'Most fences' reads backwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Efts are young newts, small amphibian creatures.

clue.text: Ships that are anything but slow?

explanation.surface: Vessels that are certainly not sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval force is a group of ships; fleet also means swift or nimble.

clue.text: Thickhead's obesity

parts.note: fat means thick or broad
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A dimwit's overweight condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thickhead' reads as a dunce, but splits into THICK (FAT) and HEAD (NESS, a promontory as in Loch Ness).
explanation.definitionFit: Obesity is excessive body weight, corpulence.

clue.text: Numbers incorporate river holdings

indicators.note: incorporate means take into the body, so the river goes inside the numbers

parts.note: tens are numbers
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Figures include river properties.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river much used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenures are terms or rights of holding land or office.

clue.text: Farther down the road the French turned sideways

parts.note: farther down the road is an idiom for in the future, at a later time

indicators.note: turned means the French article is reversed

parts.note: la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Further along, the French took a side turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means to the side, as a lateral move.

clue.text: Elegant-and repeatedly made to pay for it

parts.note: re as a prefix means again
someone fined is made to pay a penalty

explanation.surface: A stylish person keeps getting penalised for their style.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined means cultured and polished in manner.

clue.text: For the climber coldly cutting in

definitions.text: For the climber coldly cutting in

parts.words: For the climber coldly cutting in
parts.note: a mountaineer's tool that chops into frozen surfaces

explanation.surface: A climber interrupts someone with a frosty manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers use this pick to cut steps in frozen slopes.

clue.text: Ring and point out there's a choice

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of point are rearranged

explanation.surface: Phone and explain that there is an alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests phoning; it is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is an alternative one may choose.

clue.text: One exceptionally old should be a revered figure

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: exceptionally means in an unusual way, so the letters of old are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone extremely aged ought to be honoured.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an object of worship or admiration.

clue.text: Squander money when in low spirits

explanation.surface: Throw cash away when feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: To blue money is old British slang for spending it recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue money is to waste it; feeling blue means feeling sad.

clue.text: Conclude gold and black may be approved of

parts.note: to end is to conclude
or is the heraldic word for gold
sable is the heraldic word for black

explanation.surface: Finish with gold and black and it may win approval.
explanation.walkthrough: OR and SABLE are heraldic colours, gold and black.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endorsable can be signed off or supported.

clue.text: The woman's no artist!

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: She is certainly no painter!
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nora is a female first name, so stands for a woman.

clue.text: An uncharitable fellow wanting to find himself?

explanation.surface: A selfish man who is on a quest for his own identity.
explanation.definitionFit: An egotist seeks his own advantage; the second reading is someone searching for his own self.
